## Appearing in "Our Secret Wars, Part One"

**Featured Characters:**

*   [Captain America (Steve Rogers)](/wiki/Steven_Rogers_(Earth-616) "Steven Rogers (Earth-616)")

## Synopsis for "Our Secret Wars, Part One"

_A young man named David Colton witnessed the [9/11](/wiki/9/11 "9/11") terrorist attack. Compelled by the attack, and unwilling to turn his back on the suffering and inhumanity seen from America and across the planet, Colton tried to enlist in the U.S. Army. However, the recruiter cannot accept him due to his frail body. Regardless, Colton managed to enlist much to his mother's disappointment, who she sees America's [war on terrorism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_on_terror "wikipedia:War on terror") more of revenge and prejudice, and is afraid of losing another son as Colton's brother Brian died in the previous Gulf War._

After a week since he was unfrozen in the modern world, Steve Rogers is at a diner where he hears a police officer having been shot by an unhinged man, who stole his motorcycle. Rogers takes action and dons his Captain America costume. Borrowing a police motorcycle, Rogers pursues the shooter who is heading for the United Nations building. The shooter, who is revealed to have skills serving in the military, tries to shake off Rogers but the hero then uses his shield to knock the man from his motorcycle while also revealing to have a bomb strapped to his chest. The man jumps up to his feet and runs for the UN. When the guards at the gate try to stop him, the man prepares to detonate his explosive vest. But Rogers arrives and talks down the man from blowing himself up.

Rogers recognizes the man to be suffering from trauma while in service, and the man reveals that he was a Second Lieutenant who served in two tours in the Persian Gulf and had suffered the loss of everyone he knew died in his service, and believing that they died for nothing for people who do not care for them. Rogers consoles the man by telling him what he is doing is wrong and only brings more death, which succeeds in pacifying him. Iron Man soon arrives and electronically disables the bomb. After the world-be-suicide bomber is arrested, Rogers and Iron Man discuss about the recent events. Iron Man offers Rogers membership to the Avengers, but Rogers politely declines and speaks of his intentions to re-enlist in the U.S. Army.

_Colton was soon being bullied by his fellow recruits for his frail physiques. Despite the abuses, Colton remains persistent, believing that he can be someone like his role model, Steve Rogers. One night, Colton's drill instructor forcefully pulls him out from his bed and physically assaults him, deeming him an embarrassment and a "deficit" in the battlefield. Colton tries to fight back but is subsequently hospitalized. He was soon visited by an instructor who sympathized with Colton before offering him a chance to "cure his asthma"._

At the Pentagon, Rogers proves his identity to General Thaddeus Ross. Though Ross is curious to ask Rogers why he wishes to serve again even when the Second World War is long over. Rogers answers that everyone he knew back in his time, his friends such as his partner James "Bucky" Barnes and his parents, are now dead and the only thing that matters to him now is serving with the men and women in the Army. Ross is left understandable and he welcomes Rogers back to the U.S. Armed Forces.

Later, Captain America helps the Fantastic Four in stopping a giant monster by apprehending the creature's master, the Mole Man. Afterwards, Rogers talks with Reed Richards to discuss information about Victor von Doom, the recent and current ruler of Latveria. Rogers reveals to Richards that his superiors are assembling a covert strike force, which includes Rogers, to Latveria to rescue U.S. diplomats after the U.S. embassy in Latveria was attacked during Doom's coup. While Richards is very familiar with Doom and offers the Four to help in the rescue, but Rogers respectfully declines as such a very public and American superpowered team were to intervene on foreign ground it will stir international controversy; the world is wary of superhumans to the point of the U.N. planning to vote a resolution banning "extra-powered beings" from military operations on foreign soil. Despite that, no country is willing to halt their super-soldier programs, and the U.S. is no different.

Richards divulges what he knows about Doom: he was once Richards' colleague in college and a volatile yet brilliant man who was scarred in a terrible accident that led to his expulsion. After a few years, Doom reappeared in his home country and overthrew its despotic ruler, and assumed control of Latveria. While a hateful and egotistical tyrant, he was not like Adolf Hitler that Rogers fought against; he had no hate for groups of people, but at himself for being unable to save his parents. His ego was all about control and punishment for anyone who gets in his way. Richards knows Doom's weakness is his own ego, and offers Rogers a device that could disable Doom's armor. Richards then shows Rogers a Captain America figure which his father gifted to him when he was eight years old and expresses how he and others grew up learning about the Captain's exploits to fight evil, and is now glad to see the world need the hero again.

Rogers suited up in a new uniform for the covert mission. Ross debriefs Rogers about Marius Wolf, the leader of the Latverian resistance, who is willing to help the Americans to rescue the hostages. So far Doom hasn't been making demands for the hostages. Rogers is then introduced to the strike team, SEAL Team X aka the "Howling Commandos", consisting of Terry "Chill" Mendoza, Julie Slate, and (to Rogers' surprise) David Colton, the modern day Captain America.

## Solicit Synopsis

A NEW ERA FOR CAPTAIN AMERICA BEGINS HERE!

• While Captain America slumbered in ice, the world changed – for better and for worse. Steve Rogers awakens to a reality where battles are fought in the shadows through secrets and subterfuge, and villains aren’t so easy to identify.

• When a fledgling dictator named Victor Von Doom conquers Latveria, Steve faces a critical decision: adapt to a new kind of warfare, or forge his own path? And what will the choice he makes in the past mean for his future?

• Experience the untold tale of Captain America’s first encounter with Doctor Doom as Chip Zdarsky and Valerio Schiti team up for a game-changing new era of CAPTAIN AMERICA!

## Notes

*   There is multiple inconsistencies that make it unclear exactly when this story takes place

*   According to General Ross' assistant, this story takes place the week after Captain America was found by the Avengers in [Avengers #4](/wiki/Avengers_Vol_1_4 "Avengers Vol 1 4").

*   In another instance, Captain America joins the Fantastic Four against the Mole Man and his monster in what appears to be their first battle from [Fantastic Four #1](/wiki/Fantastic_Four_Vol_1_1 "Fantastic Four Vol 1 1")

*   Iron Man is wearing his [Iron Man Armor Model 2](/wiki/Iron_Man_Armor_Model_2 "Iron Man Armor Model 2") armor.

*   The Fantastic Four appear in the [Fantasticar MK I](/wiki/Fantasticar_MK_I "Fantasticar MK I"), isn't used until some time after their battle with the Mole Man.

*   A young David Colton is present during the attack on the Twin Towers in New York on 9/11 in 2001.

*   There are several references to the Taliban and the wars in the Middle East.
